# The "Hawks"
The [bold]Colonial Protection Organization[/bold] (CPO), known to the average servicemember as the [bold]Hawks[/bold], is the faction within the UA's militaries that believes in crushing resistance with overwhelming force and restoring the military's glory through victory.
## History - The CPO was founded in 2108, soon after the UA itself, by those enraged at the handling of the Torin Prime colony and the J'Har rebel insurgency. They believed the Outer Rim Defense Force's refusal to destroy the J'Har headquarters, for fear of civilian casualties, let the rebellion take root and ultimately cost more lives than a swift strike would have. - After early successes, it fell dormant through the quieter decades of the 2110s to 2140s for lack of leadership and military victories to rally around. - The wars over Three World Empire colonies and the Dog War brought it back. When the UA accepted peace at the Red Line in 2163, the CPO was furious, and its new hardline leadership drew fierce devotion. Its narrow focus on the USCM, however, has cost it much of its support in other branches, such as the LACN, where the Doves have flourished instead.
## Ideology [italic]These are the faction's general attitudes. Individual members may hold only some of them.[/italic] - [bold]Alignment[/bold]: traditional, force projection, military dominance and glory. Non-corporate. - A servicemember's life is worth more than an entire colony's. Ammunition, supplies and uncooperative civilians are expendable; your comrades are not. - Progress requires sacrifice, but troops should be sacrificed only once every other resource, including the local population, has been spent. - If locals won't cooperate, burn them out. - Shock and awe is an enemy's one chance to learn to cooperate. - Victories keep the military's standing and funding secure. Never shy away from a fight.
## Internal Divisions The CPO looks monolithic, held together by forceful, top-down leadership. Beneath that, some regional commanders and troops resent its overwhelming control and narrow focus on the USCM, and feel the organization has grown too centralized and stagnant.
## Reputation - Its message of strength, control and swift retribution appeals to many officials on an unstable frontier, though some back it only quietly. CPO-aligned officers often form tight cliques that share intelligence and support each other without openly declaring their allegiance. - Its "containment directives" send heavily armed platoons against insurgent hotspots, pirate strongholds and suspected CLF safehouses. Whole settlements suspected of harboring dissidents have been flattened, and pirate fleets destroyed even as they tried to surrender. Pirate activity in several regions has dropped sharply and governors report fewer distress calls, but the locals remain as resentful and afraid of the USCM as ever. - Surprisingly, some CPO-aligned forces have begun forming black ops teams to eliminate hidden CLF cells and UPP saboteurs before they can strike. - Its disregard for civilians has turned many colonists against the UA, who now see the UA military as an occupying force, and has prompted several investigations into the CPO.
## Relations - [textlink="The Doves" link="CMUGuideLoreUADoves"]: bitter rivals. The Hawks see the Doves as naive and irresponsible, wasting soldiers' lives on potentially hostile civilians and leaving insurgencies to grow. They also fear that cheap humanitarian work costs the military funding that victories would bring, and that less funding means more dead troops. - [textlink="The Magpies" link="CMUGuideLoreUAMagpies"]: distrustful. The Hawks accept UA government-owned companies, but fear foreign corporations, above all [textlink="Weyland-Yutani" link="CMUGuideLoreWY"], a Three World Empire company with its own executives aboard UA warships.
